newsitem.title: GERMANY: VEBA ends telcoms alliance with C&W.
newsitem.headline: VEBA ends telcoms alliance with C&W.

text.p: Germany's Veba AG said on Friday it would end its strategic alliance with Britain's Cable and Wireless, setting the stage for a likely reshuffle in global telecommunications alliances.

Veba said it would buy back Cable and Wireless' 45 percent stake in Veba's telecoms subsidiary Vebacom for 2.21 billion marks. At the same time, Cable and Wireless plans to obtain Veba's 50 percent stake in C&W Europe for 90 million marks.
Speculation that the Vebacom alliance, formed in 1995, was about to collapse mounted earlier this week when industry sources said Veba offered to buy back the C&W stake.

Veba said different business strategies were to blame for the deal's collapse, with Veba planning to invest more heavily in Germany while Cable & Wireless planned to concentrate on its home market in Britain.
But Veba said it planned to keep a 10.4 percent stake in Cable & Wireless. A bank trustee will hold Cable & Wireless' stake in the venture during a search for new partners.

Veba also said the collapse of the Vebacom alliance will not impact its telecoms joint-venture called "o.tel.o" with German energy group RWE. The joint venture on Friday received German cartel office approval.
